main_text.p: namq; noftri corporis actionem laedi pofe,nisi proxima eius causa prius sit læsa, apud omnes medicos in confesso est.ʼ Proxima autem causa actionis similarium partium est earu sanitas: quæ Galeno pasim, & præsertim libro de Optima corporis Constitutione,& primo de Sanitate tuenda,nihil est aliud quam temperamentum. Igitur nulla partis similaris actio laedi poteft, nisi prius temperamentu eius sit læsum. Quod autem corporis similaris actio omnis temperamento debeatur,non negat Fernelius libr.de Abditis rerum causis secundo.Quū igitur partis similaris actio bona temperamento debeatur, malam contra ad intemperiem referri, ac pertinere conseques est: quandoquidem contrariorum eadem est doctrina. Itaq; nulla similaris partis actio laedi,impediriue poteft,illefo temperamento.Quare prima Fernelij ratio uana omnino est.Quæ poftea cofequitur, nempe multorum uentriculum nec acetum, neq; finapi ferre poffe,non maiorem facit fidem.Nā quod nonnullorum uentriculus, nec acetū,neq; finapi,aut aliud fimile acre & mordax perferre haud queat, non est materia uentriculi,sed excellens sentiendi uis,qua talis

page.notes: Left margin: small marks beside lines 18 to 27 (roughly "·s", "·ss", "ıı", "ıs", "ı") are unclear and may be printed reference signs or stains; not transcribed. Running head and "IN ABDITAS RER. NATVR." are uncertain at "RER." and "NATVR." Faint marks at lower left (a possible signature) are illegible and not transcribed. Several words have a doubtful long s or ligature: "confesso", "posse", "conseques" are transcribed with plain s. Words with [?] were not marked because the scan is clear enough at those points. "illefo" in the scan may read "illeso". Sentence on line 19 contains "impediriue" as printed.
